description:
## Finding (corrected 2026-11-18)
The original premise was wrong: squash merges are not what keeps the ledger from advancing. corpus-event-bridge.yml, corpus-reconciler.yml and scripts/publication/reconciler.py fed publication/ledger.json, the ledger of the publication control plane that site-split-51-publication-retirement removed from core in October (#3096). That file has never existed on published-results; the reconciler only validates and prints, never writes, and nothing reads its output. The hourly reconciler always reports no events. They were missed by the retirement's delete list and survived only because the reconciler workflow imports the script.

The publication ledger in use is publication/ledger-seed.json on develop, re-cut from published-results by seed-corpus.yml and make ledger-seed-recut, and read by the corpus_bijection attestation and scripts/site_inputs.py. It is current and unaffected.

## Change
Delete both workflows, scripts/publication/reconciler.py, tests/unit/scripts/publication/test_reconciler.py, tests/unit/workflows/test_corpus_event_bridge.py and the reconciler case in test_override_companion_exclusion.py; remove their rows from docs/internal/dev-loop-property-ledger.md, tests/unit/ledger_cutover_files.txt and quality/windows-antipatterns-baseline.json, and record in the property ledger why the property stays covered.

## Guardrails
- ledger-seed.json, create_ledger_seed.py, check_corpus_bijection.py, validator_parity.py and the seed-corpus workflow stay.
- No change to published-results or repository settings.
